cards.explanation: The answer is to go around the land of Edom. The text says they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea "…in order to bypass the land of Edom." So the passage itself gives us the reason for the route. I've taken the long way around my own kitchen to dodge a pan I burned, so I get it, friends.

The answer is True. The text says the people "…grew impatient on the journey". Their patience ran out somewhere along the way. I know that feeling, friends. I once got antsy waiting for a batch to cool, and that's a ten minute wait.

The answer is Moses. The people "…spoke against God and against Moses…" and Moses is Israel's leader. So the complaint went to God and to the man leading them. I think that's a tough spot to stand in, and I bet Moses felt it.
The answer is bread or water, friends. The people say, "There is no bread or water…" That's the complaint, word for word. I'll just say it: a kitchen with no bread or water would make even me grumpy.

The answer is venomous snakes. The text says, "…the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died." This is the heavy turn in the story, friends. It's a serious moment, and the next verses show where it goes.

The answer is sinned. The people tell Moses, "We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you." They said it out loud and named it. That's not an easy thing to do, friends, and I've had to do it more than once myself.

The answer is to intercede so the LORD takes the snakes away. The people say, "Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us." To intercede is to speak to God for someone else. They asked Moses to be that voice, and the text says, "So Moses interceded for the people."

The answer is a fiery serpent, friends. The LORD tells Moses, "Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole." Picture Moses hearing that one. I bet he had questions, and I'd have had a whole list. But the text says he did it: he made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole (Numbers 21:9).
The answer is looks. The LORD says, "When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live." Looking is the whole thing, friends. Just look, and live.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live." It says anyone, not just the first person. Every bitten person who looked would live, and there was no line to stand in or number to take.
